label: F-ed9f89

findings.note: Plan D3 specifies `string QuotaKeyOf(string model) => string.Empty` on IReviewerRuntime word for word, so the string key at ReviewerRuntime.cs is the decided design, not a defect.

TheAgyQuotaReportPicksTheResetTests.cs:30-35 `Edited` parses a new private tree from the immutable input string and returns a new string, which is the plan's 'constructed from a real one' fixture pattern, not shared-state mutation.

`ReviewerOutcome.Ok` carries a `NormalisedReview` (ReviewerExecutor.cs:106) and a malformed answer is the separate `Unparseable` outcome (:201); plan D4/D5 decide that an `Ok` lifts, and a parked key's rows are not launched at all because `CanRun` excludes them.

The finding admits the standing entry survives (`Nothing` at QuotaCooldowns.cs:415 leaves it, and `Applied` drops only expired entries); not parking an undecided refusal on an Available or CannotCheck gauge is exactly plan D5/D10.
Plan D4's fail-open contract decides that reads answer 'no cooldown' and warn once per process, and only refused writes go to the notice path; QuotaCooldowns.cs:183-195 does exactly that.

The probes do run one after another (QuotaCooldowns.cs:385-388), but only agy keys with a known group probe (AntigravityRuntime.cs:188 skips unknown ones), so the worst case is 3×30 s, not the claimed 'ten keys, five minutes'.

PanelService builds every store inline, including `new UsageLedger(settings.DataDir)` on the line above the new `QuotaCooldowns`, so there is no DI root being bypassed; a second instance would share the file and its lock safely, and other consumers are explicitly out of scope (D12).
Plan D5 puts `ReadResetAsync` on IReviewerRuntime and has `AfterRoundAsync` call it once per key outside the lock, which is what QuotaCooldowns.cs:429 does.
Plan D3 explicitly chooses 'one explicit, measured table' over a prefix rule (the Argon reason) and decides that unknown families get their own key with no gauge-based parking.

Refusals are pre-filtered by `Qualifies`, so `Spent == false` never reaches `chosen` (QuotaCooldowns.cs:409,425); all refusals in a group share one quota key, so they read the same gauge group, and the finding describes no concrete wrong outcome.

The CRLF claim is wrong because `StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries` strips `\r` (AgyError.cs:33), but its aside is real: an AGY_ERROR whose JSON spans several lines, as in the issue's own sample, fails `JsonDocument.Parse` per line and falls back to the word scan.

`AtomicFile.Write` discards its temp file on any exception and removes orphaned temps before writing (AtomicFile.cs Write/catch/RemoveOrphanedTemps), and the lock stream is disposed by `using` (QuotaCooldowns.cs:309).
`NoteOf` passes the reason through `VendorReason.Written`, which is `Redaction.SafeText`, after the executor has already redacted both streams; this is plan D2/D4 as written.
Plan D4 decides 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)'; PanelService.StandingCooldown follows that decision.

This duplicates index 5 with an accurate bound (up to about 90 s when all three agy groups are spent at QuotaCooldowns.cs:385-388); running the probes concurrently is cheap, but the case is rare next to a multi-minute round.
Rounding up is the plan's D9 decision ('rounded UP as resetWords.ts does'), and `(minutes + 59) / 60` is already the integer ceiling the suggested fix would compute.

missed: AgyError.Parse reads AGY_ERROR one line at a time (AgyError.cs:33-45), so the multi-line AGY_ERROR JSON shown in the issue's own sample from the owner's PC never parses; it falls back to the word scan with Spent=null, and a spent quota is parked only if the gauge confirms it.
summary: Most of the 16 findings ask for things the plan explicitly decided (string keys, a static group table, no cache, fail-open reads, the probe on the runtime, rounding up) or misread code that already handles the case (`Ok` already means a parsed review, redaction is applied, temp files are cleaned up). Only the sequential-probe point (minor, raised twice) and a buried multi-line AGY_ERROR aside are partly real, and the review flagged a 'Blocking' architecture issue that matches the codebase's existing pattern.
